title: Exploiting relevance, coverage, and novelty for query-focused multi-document summarization
research_question: Can query-focused multi-document summaries be improved by jointly modeling dependent relevance, content coverage, novelty, and topic balance rather than treating sentence relevance independently?
methodology: The paper proposes PRCN, an unsupervised extractive framework built from PLSA and PHITS that uses a query-aware reference topic model to estimate dependent sentence relevance and topic coverage. Relevance and coverage are represented probabilistically, while additional document-side and query-side relevance and novelty features are constructed explicitly; model parameters are estimated with expectation maximization. A greedy sentence-selection procedure imposes topic and query balance while constructing the final summary. The approach is evaluated on the DUC 2005 and DUC 2006 query-focused multi-document summarization benchmarks using ROUGE measures.

key_findings.finding: The paper argues that sentence utility is dependent on what has already been selected or seen, and PRCN therefore replaces the usual independent-relevance assumption with probabilistic dependent relevance.
key_findings.section: Section 1, Introduction; Section 3, Problem Definition and Solution

key_findings.finding: PRCN jointly represents relevance, topic coverage, and novelty rather than optimizing query relevance alone.
The sentence-selection stage uses a greedy balancing procedure intended to preserve suitable proportions of document and query topics while limiting redundancy.
key_findings.section: Section 5, Feature Construction and Topic Balance Imposition

key_findings.finding: Experiments on DUC 2005 and DUC 2006 report that PRCN outperforms the compared methods on ROUGE-2 and ROUGE-W by a statistically described significant margin.
The approach is unsupervised and extractive, so its coverage and novelty decisions are made by selecting source sentences rather than generating new text.

limitations: Evaluation is restricted to the DUC 2005 and DUC 2006 query-focused summarization benchmarks, so generalization beyond those news-oriented datasets is not established by the reported experiments.
The method operates on a static document collection and does not model temporal state transitions or supersession of previously summarized work items.
The method is extractive and therefore does not address factual support problems introduced by free-form generation.
ROUGE-2 and ROUGE-W measure lexical overlap and do not directly evaluate evidence completeness, lifecycle-state correctness, or joint omission and repetition.
The approach depends on latent-topic and bag-of-words-style preprocessing assumptions, including stopword removal and stemming.
No publicly released implementation is identified in the article.
raw_claims: A useful query-focused summary must balance relevance to the query with coverage of the source documents.
Selecting one sentence can change the utility of selecting another sentence later.
PRCN models relevance and coverage within a common probabilistic framework.
The query is incorporated into a reference topic model used to estimate dependent relevance.
Novelty features are used to discourage redundant information.
The model includes features defined from both document and query perspectives.
A greedy selection algorithm is used to maintain topic balance while choosing summary sentences.
Model estimation uses an expectation-maximization procedure.
The evaluation uses the DUC 2005 and DUC 2006 query-focused summarization datasets.
The reported experiments favor PRCN over the compared methods on ROUGE-2 and ROUGE-W.
